hero.titulo: Crypto tax advisory and crypto income tax returns in Spain
hero.entrada: An automated report is the starting point, never the deliverable. We reconcile your exchanges, wallets and protocols, review by hand what software would settle with a default value, and write down where every figure comes from.

clasificador.titulo: Which of these situations looks like yours?
clasificador.entrada: A hundred thousand transactions on Solana, a portfolio spread across six exchanges or a three-year-old loss to offset. Your trading is unique; your questions aren’t: almost all of them end up in these three.
clasificador.otraCosa: None of these? Tell us about your trading

perfiles.titulo: Who we advise and what each profile needs
perfiles.entrada: Whoever gets here is usually in one of these situations. The level of detail and the urgency change; what doesn’t change is that every figure has to be explainable.

A.descripcion: Thousands of transactions, several exchanges, DeFi across several chains. You worry an automated report will leave you exposed.

B.descripcion: Shares, funds and some crypto. You want to file correctly without having to learn the jargon.

C.descripcion: You already have a letter from the AEAT on your desk. You need to know what to do and by when.

D.descripcion: An accounting or advisory firm without crypto expertise. You need technical support and professional backing.

metodo.titulo: All your sources, one tax report
intro: We prepare your crypto tax report from all your data sources. We import the history of every exchange, such as Binance, Coinbase or Kraken; of your wallets, such as MetaMask or Ledger; and public addresses on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana or any other network, including transactions on DeFi protocols such as Uniswap or Aave.

Then we rebuild your portfolio transaction by transaction. We identify transfers between your own wallets, remove duplicates and spam tokens, assign the euro value of every movement and calculate gains and losses with the FIFO method applied by the Spanish Tax Agency. Whatever software would settle with a default value is reviewed by hand by an advisor.
The result is a single report, traceable line by line, with the figures ready for your income tax return (Form 100) and, where applicable, for Form 721 and Form 714.
pasos: We remove spam, duplicates and transfers between your wallets

metodo.mas: And any other source: CSV exports, API connections or public addresses on any network.

informe.titulo: A report that stands up to the AEAT

puntos: Every line links to its transaction detail.

informe.vistaPrevia: This is the results page: a summary of what you file, which is what you ultimately need to know. Behind it come the pages that reconstruct, transaction by transaction, how each figure is reached; long, but written so that anyone reviewing them can follow, starting with the tax authority.

items.q: Do I have to declare my crypto if I haven’t cashed out to euros?
items.a: Yes, if you’ve swapped one for another. Converting BTC into USDT, for example, is an exchange of assets and produces a capital gain or loss even if you never withdraw euros. If you only bought and hold, that isn’t taxed in income tax, but there may be reporting obligations: form 721 if on 31 December you hold more than 50.000 € in crypto with custodians outside Spain, and form 714 if you are liable for wealth tax.

items.q: Which method is used to calculate the gain?
items.a: FIFO: the first units of a crypto asset you acquired are the first ones deemed sold. The gain or loss is the difference between the disposal value and the acquisition value of those units, fees included. Applying it properly requires the full history: if an old purchase is missing, its acquisition cost can’t be justified.

items.q: Are staking, DeFi and airdrops taxed?
items.a: Yes, though not all in the same way. The Directorate General of Taxes treats staking rewards as investment income and airdrops as a capital gain not arising from a disposal. Swaps on a protocol are exchanges of assets. For liquidity provision and lending, the treatment depends on how each protocol works, and that’s where automated reports tend to get it wrong.

items.q: Why isn’t Koinly or CoinTracking enough?
items.a: Because software doesn’t decide: it applies a default. It counts transfers between your own wallets as sales, leaves purchases without an acquisition cost or values spam tokens as if they were real. They are good tools to start with. We start from their output or from the raw data, review transaction by transaction and write down the criterion behind each figure.

items.q: What do you need from me and how long does it take?
items.a: The CSV files or read-only access to your exchanges and the public addresses of your wallets. With that we run an initial diagnosis. Time and price depend on the volume and complexity of the portfolio: from 3–5 days for simple activity to 2–3 weeks for a multi-chain portfolio with thousands of transactions. These are estimates; we give you a specific one once we see your data.

faq.q: Why don’t you charge by number of transactions?
faq.a: Because the work isn’t counting transactions, it’s matching sources. A thousand buys on one exchange are processed like ten; what takes time is following the same asset as it moves from an exchange to a wallet and on to a protocol.

faq.q: Does the price depend on how much I made?
faq.a: No. We charge for the reconciliation work, not the result. A portfolio with losses takes the same work as one with gains, and it’s often the one most worth documenting properly.

faq.q: What if my portfolio turns out to be more complex than I thought?
faq.a: We tell you before we start. The tier is confirmed with your data in front of us, not halfway through, so the price you accept is the price you pay.

faq.q: How much does it cost to reply to a request from the tax agency?
faq.a: With an open request, rebuilding your figures costs €150 more in each tier: €400, €500, €600 and from €850, VAT included. The difference is the deadline: your case jumps the queue and is worked against the date set by the tax agency. The written reply and representation before the AEAT are quoted separately as soon as we’ve read the notice, usually the same day.

faq.q: What do I need to get a quote?
faq.a: The list of platforms, wallets and protocols you’ve used and the tax years you’re worried about is enough. If you already have the exports or a Koinly or CoinTracking report, even better: we can be more precise.
